newsitem.title: ITALY: First Italian troops arrive in violence-hit Naples.
newsitem.headline: First Italian troops arrive in violence-hit Naples.

text.p: The first Italian troops arrived in the southern port of Naples on Sunday following a government decision to send the army to help quell a wave of violence sparked by fighting between mafia clans.
Some 300 troops arrived in buses, trucks and jeeps to prepare to take up surveillance and security duties in and around the city on Monday.
Italy's centre-left government said last Friday it would send 500 soldiers to take over guard duties around Naples, freeing police to focus on halting a wave of mob violence that has swept the city.

The decision to send in troops was announced last Monday after a weekend of terror in which two suspected mobsters were mown down in broad daylight and a number of innocent bystanders, including an eight-year-old girl, were hurt in shootouts.
Some 86 people have been killed and dozens injured since the start of the year as rival clans of the Camorra, the Naples mafia, have fought each other for territorial control.

The battles have increasingly spread to the city's streets and there was public outrage last month after a young woman was killed by a stray bullet as she walked home with her six-year-old son in an affluent neighbourhood.
Italian newspapers on Sunday published maps highlighting where troops would be stationed, including the law courts, the jail, the synagogue and a number of foreign consular offices.
Local merchants have feared that the presence of troops in the city's historic centre would hurt a tourist boom carefully nurtured over the past four years.

Italy has used troops before in various parts of the country to quell crime waves. Soldiers are still stationed on the southern island of Sicily five years after they were called in following the murder of two leading magistrates.
